label: text
text: PRINCE DAHNI OF SIAM IN HONGKONG.

label: text
text: TIFFIN AT HOTEL

label: text
text: Mr. T. J. Bagram (honorary Consul in Hongkong for Siam) and Mrs. Bugram were hosts at the Hongkong Hotel at tiffin today in honour of H.H. Prince Dahni and H.S.H. Princess Sipban, of Siam, and H.E. the Governor (Sir Cecil Clementi) and Lady Clementi.

label: text
text: Prince Dahni, a younger son of the King of Siam, is making a tour to inquire into education. He will have to report to his father when he returns home.

label: text
text: Graduate of a British University, the Prince visited the Vice Chancellor of the Hongkong University (Mr. W. W. Hornell) and the Director of Education (Mr. A. E. Wood) during his stay here a few weeks ago. Since then he has visited Manila and then returned here.

label: text
text: Among those present were Major-General C. C. and Mrs. Luard, Rear-Admiral A. J. B. Stirling, the Hon. Mr. W. T. and Mrs. Southorn, Sir Shou-son and Lady Chow, the Hon. Mr. C. McI. Messer, the Hon. Mr. H. T. and Mrs. Creasy, the Hon. Mr. J. H. Kemp, the Hon. Mr. E. D. C. Wolfe, the Hon. Mr. E. R. Hallifax, the Hon. Dr. R. H. Kotewall, the Hon. Dr. W. V. M. and Mrs. Koch, the Hon. Mr. D. G. M. Bernard, the Hon. Mr. H. W. and Mrs. Bird, the Hon. Mr. A. O. Lang, Sir Henry Cowper Gollan, Mr. Justice J. R. and Mrs. Wood, Col. C. & Mrs. Russell-Brown, R.E. Senator and Madame C. de Albuquerque e Castro, Mr. R. C. Tredwell, Mr. A. H. Barlow, Mr. and Mrs. W. E. L. Shenton, Mr. and Mrs. A. H. Ferguson, Commander C. Dowbiggin, A.D.C., Mr. B. Forster (private secretary to H.E.), Pay Lt. E. D. T. Churcher, R.N. and Mr. Luang Visavakum.

label: text
text: Mr. Bagram proposed the toast of H.M. King George, the drinking of which was accompanied by the National Anthem.

label: text

label: paragraph_title
text: PEAK WATER.

label: text
text: ENGINES KEEP PACE WITH DEMAND.

label: text
text: A few weeks ago, it will be remembered, restriction in hours of water supply service to the Peak were removed, the Water Authority notifying that if the consumption was reduced to something like 75 per cent of what it was in the normal course, such full supply could be continued; otherwise that it might be necessary to cut off supplies without warning, if there was a danger of the tanks being seriously depleted.

label: text
text: Upon enquiry this morning, the "China Mail" was informed that the two engines in operation had been able to keep pace with the demand and it was hoped—providing consumers continued to eliminate waste—to continue the service.

label: text
text: The Peak and higher levels supply throughout the winter will be dependent on the two engines in question and if either went out of action, restriction would have to be continued. The main engine broken up by the boulder crash would be repaired before the hot season next year.

label: paragraph_title
text: ISLAND OF KISSES

label: text
text: “UNCHINESE” VILLAIN

label: text
text: "Made up" as a Chinese villain, one of the screen actors in the George Jacoby Co. of Germany, now in Hongkong, was the hero in the eyes of the crowds of Chinese who gathered in Queen's Road Central this morning to witness the unusual sight of taking a film here.

label: text
text: Not many props were in use and not many "of the spectators understood what "out on location" meant" till they spotted the two machines in the distance.

label: text
text: A motor 'car with 'public vehicle' on the licence was drawn up outside a 'goldsmith's establishment and a street ricsha was standing near.

label: text
text:
Herine "Lost" Here.
As explained in Tuesday's "China Mail," Mr. George Jacoby (who "directed, "Qno Vadia!") is making two pictures for Universal Pictures Corporation, "with scenes in Hongkong and Shanghai. They are "Island of Kisses" and "The Woman Without a Name."

label: text
text: In the “Island of Kisses,” the heroine becomes “lost” and is discovered in Hongkong.

label: text
text: This probably accounted for the fact that when a "Mail" reporter reached the spot there, was no lady there ready to "do her stuff."

label: text
text: The location is that part of Queen's Road, in the Chinese business centre, just beyond the old fire station.

label: text
text: What the Stars were Doing.

label: text
text: High cheekbones, “villainous eyes” and prominent, protruding teeth a la Lon Chaney were the principal features in the make-up of the man in the car, with the Chinese chauffeur in his seat behind the wheel.

label: text
text: "Shooting" had not actually begun and the actor—unlike any Chinese—was listening to an exhortation by another member of the company.

label: text
text: Another “star” sat nonchalantly in the ricsha awaiting developments. He gave the appearance of an ordinary non-Chinese foreman in workaday clothes.

label: text
text: A gentleman in shirtsleeves, apparently directing operations, was examining the inside of the car.

label: text
text:
Just where the China New Year bazaar "begins" the two camera men were posted with their machines on the tripods.
Around them clustered two hundred Chinese, one of whom was heard to remark: Oh! why hang about when these P.W.D. surveyors are taking measurements every day.

label: text
text: His friend disagreed. Those machines, he argued, must be for the purpose of registering the speed of the car for traffic requirements.

label: text
text: This sort of chatter was general but there were not a few who understood what the business was about.

label: text
text: With the Chinese aversion to being photographed, the “China Mail’s” advice to the company is that to get a clear view—it was 100 yards from the machine to the car—turn the “shoot” on the crowd, pretend to “take,” and you will not be obstructed.

text: WUCHANG LOST?

label: paragraph_title
text: WU PEI-FU REPORTED WOUNDED.

label: text
text: LAPEST INTELLIGENCE

label: text
text: Several sources, both foreign and native in Shanghai and elsewhere, claim to have been advised that the southern Nationalists are pressing forwards in their campaign against Wu Pei-fu and the northerners.

label: text
text: Hitherto the "Wah Tsz Yat Po" has never definitely stated that the city of Wuchang has been captured by the Canton troops. Té-day it published a cable that Wuchang has fallen.

label: text
text: From the gist of the messages to hand it appears that the northerners have been unable to hold their line and that the Nationalists are constantly hammering away on different sectors.

label: text
text: Two reports state that Wu Petu was wounded and that he has gone to Hanyang.

label: text
text: Wuchang is on the southern bank of the Yangtse River. The difficulty of making out conflict

label: paragraph_title
text: STRONG POLICY.

label: paragraph_title
text: Urged on Britain in China.

label: paragraph_title
text: PLEA FOR INTERVENTION

label: text
text: Time to Show Britain is in

label: text
text: London, Sept. 1.

label: text
text: Urging a strong policy on the part of the Powers in view of recent anti-foreign developments in China, the Daily Telegraph says that the so-called conciliation, which is actually nerveless submission, has only made the position worse.

label: text
text: It expresses the opinion that Great Britain is the one Powerable to bring the United States and Japan together with herself and others in a common policy of intervention in some form which is amply warranted by the ghastliness of the tragedy at present being enacted in China, whither, the paper suggests Great Britain should send a special Plenipotentiary for instance, the Marquis of Reading, who will show that Great Britain is in earnest. Reuter.

label: text
text:
ing intelligence is referred to, editorially, on page 6. It remains to be seen if the Cantonese, having taken Wuchang, will cross the river to Hankow and Hanyang.
Wu Pei-fu holds the (Chinese) Yangtse flotilla. But with the fortunes of war against him it is likely that the gunboats will remain “neutral.”

label: paragraph_title
text: Capture Contradicted.

label: text
text: The Canton Information: Bureau's official claim that Hankow and Wuchang were captured on August 26, has proved to be false. Up to the present there is no confirmation of the Japanese reports that Wu Pei-fu has been wounded or that his troops have been defeated or demoralised. On the contrary a wire from Hankow on the evening of August 30 states that the attacks of the southerners on August 29 were successfully repulsed.

label: text
text: The capture of an enemy spy on the evening of August 29, elicited the information that "another attack had been planned for August 80. As a result of this information, Wu Pei-fu moved, first launching an offensive the results of which have not yet been received.

label: text
text: Chinese continue to flock in to the Hankow concessions in very large numbers with household goods and valuables.

label: text
text: Later:

label: text
text:
A Japanese despatch from Han-
kow states that the southerners
entered Wuchang last night.—

label: text
text: ALLEGED INCREASES.

label: text
text: Further eulogies have been received by the “China Mail” from tenants who allege increases of rent by owners

label: text
text: Flowery tributes are not wanted, it should be stated. Correspondents are invited to state facts which can serve as a guide towards forming an opinion as to whether decontrol as from July 1 has had any appreciable effect.

label: text
text: A Chinese correspondent, to preserve secrecy for fear of reprisals by the landlord, has cut off the beginning and end of his letter and thus taken away the signature.

label: text
text: But he fills in a measure of praise about the “esteemed paper whose editorials are so fair to the public that he prays for the continued success of great efforts” etc.

label: text
text: Shop Rent Doubled?

label: text
text:
A shopkeeper in Pottinger Street maintains that his shop has only a room for about three cubicles. He has had the tenancy for about 20 years when the rent has always been $40 a month.
(Presumably this property belonged to the late Mr. M. J. D. Stephens, since sold out of his estate).

label: text
text: Now the rent has been doubled. The writer points to his having made no profit last year; and that spring and summer of this year have passed and there is no sign of recovery.

label: paragraph_title
text: Small Figures.

label: text
text: Small figures are quoted by the tenant of the ground floor, No. 22, Swatow Lane.

label: text
text: Last year the rent was $22. The 15 per cent increase permitted last July was put into effect and he paid $25.30.

label: text
text: To get a round sum again, the writer briefly explains, the landlord has given notice of an increase of $6.70, making the total $32.

label: text
text: This tenant gives no opinion as to the fairness or otherwise of the amount demanded, but he underlines the owner's name!

label: paragraph_title
text: MISSION HOSPITALS.

label: paragraph_title
text: CANTON ORDERS INSTANT RETURN.

label: text
text: TO PROTECT FOREIGNERS.

label: text
text: After a year or so of interference with foreign missionary institutions in Canton and elsewhere, an unexpected announcement has been made by the Nationalist Government which indicates that rights will be recognised.

label: text
text: One sequel to the “strike” has been the closing down of mission hospitals on account of intimidation by the pickets.

label: text
text: The communique to hand also refers to foreign buildings occupied by the military.

label: text
text:
It will be recalled that statements have been made previously—not necessarily by any “inspired” body—that the control of certain institutions, by Chinese, would be aimed at.
The Canton Information Bureau issues the following through Reuter:—

label: text
text: Canton, Sept. 1...

label: text
text: “The Nationalist Government has ordered the office of the commander-in-chief to instruct the Wuchow authorities to immediately return the Stout Memorial Hospital at Wuchow to the American Baptist Mission for a re-opening, and also to issue peremptory orders to all Nationalist forces in Hunan and elsewhere to protect the life and property of all foreign missionaries and evacuate all mission buildings now in occupation by the military.

label: text
text: “The Government has further instructed the Miscellaneous Workers' Union to open negotiations with the authorities of the Canton Hospital for a speedy re-opening of that institution.”

label: text
text: Mr. Greenwood, the police armourer, has reported the loss of a set of tools valued at $10 from the side car of his motor cycle left at Des Vœux Road Central yester-day.

label: paragraph_title
text: KWONG HING CASE.

label: paragraph_title
text: WERE THEY AGENTS OR PRINCIPALS?

label: text
text: JUNK HEARING AGAIN

label: text
text:
The question as to whether the Kwong Hangs acted as agents or principals in the shipment of goods to Mui Kong San Wui (Kwangtung) "which did not arrive at their destination owing, it is alleged, to a piracy, came before Mr. " Justice Wood again in the Summary Court this morning.
The Ho Yuen firm claims $996.36 as the price of goods entrusted to defendant and monies on account of freight customs dues and coolie hire in respect of the shipment which the defendants failed to deliver or return to plaintiffs.

label: text
text: Mr. M. K. Lo, on behalf of the defendants, maintains that they acted throughout as... agents and not charterers.

label: text
text: Mr. J. A. Gordon Leask appeared for plaintiffs this morning, notifying a change of solicitors since the previous hearing.

label: text
text: So Chun, partner of the plaintiff firm, was cross-examined by Mr. Lo this morning. He maintained that the Kwong Hing had given an undertaking in respect of the safe delivery of the goods. The plaintiff firm, he said, had paid to the defendants 20 per cent. increase on the Customs, dues for guarantee of safe arrival in view of unsettled conditions caused by the boycott.

label: text
text: Plaintiff further stated that all the arrangements with regard to the taking on board of the cargo had been directed by the Kwong Hing firm although the junk owners had done a certain amount on their instructions

label: text
text: Mr Lo referred to the evidence which plaintiff had given in a case at the Supreme Court concerning another shipment of goods on the same junk when it had been held by the Chief Justice that not sufficient evidence had been made out for him to hold that a piracy had taken place.

label: text
text: Mr. Lo referred to what he termed "inconsistencies" in the plaintiff's evidence at that hearing and his evidence now.

label: text
text: His Honour said that he did not agree. There were no materials inconsistencies.

label: text
text: After hearing further evidence, His Honour found that the Kwong Hing firm (defendants) had only acted as agents in collecting goods. He gave judgment for defendants.

label: paragraph_title
text: BAD BEHAVIOUR.

label: paragraph_title
text: HOTEL AND CHARGE ROOM INCIDENTS.

label: text
text: EUROPEAN FINED.

label: text
text: Charges of disorderly conduct and breaking a door handle were preferred against a ship's captain, E. Bentley, at present unemployed, before Major C. Willson at the Central Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: Sergeant Pears gave evidence of defendant's misbehaviour at the King Edward Hotel yesterday afternoon where he had gone for drinks and quarreled with the bar boys and the management. Further evidence was given of violent conduct in the charge room where defendant kicked at the door handle and broke it. It was also stated that Mr. T. H. King (D.C.I.) and Captain Bloxham endeavoured to pacify him, but to no purpose.

label: text
text: The defence was that he was roughly handled by the police. He said that he had been about ten years in Hongkong during which time he had behaved well, but he objected to a European being treated like a coolist.

label: text
text: A fine of $20 was imposed and an order made for payment of $1.25 as compensation for the damage to the door handle.

label: paragraph_title
text: THE WEATHER

label: text
text:
"West or variable winds, light, fine," reads the forecast by the Observatory of weather conditions till noon tomorrow.
The forenoon report states that pressure has increased moderately over central and N.E. Japan and slightly from Indo-China to the Philippines. It has decreased moderately at Shanghai and slightly over the Loochoos. The anticyclonesa has weakened and moved eastward. It now covers Japan. The depression to the S.E. of Naha is moving northward. It may develop into a typhoon.
